topic: Strange borders countdown ending at the open India-Nepal border at Sunauli
hook: Your own country has a border so open you can walk across it before your tea cools.
title: 6 Weird Borders, and India's Has No Visa
description:
Six real borders that look fake on a map, from a US town you reach through Canada to a whole country inside another. The last one is in India: at Sunauli, Indians and Nepalis walk across a simple gate with no visa. Watch to the end to see why the open gate may be the strangest one.

#borders #geography #india
comment_prompt: Which border would you cross first?

scenes.narration: Your own country has a border so open you can walk across it before your tea cools.
scenes.headline: A Border Without A Visa

scenes.narration: No visa. No passport stamp. Just a plain gate, a rickshaw ride and a few steps into Nepal.
scenes.headline: Gate, Rickshaw, Nepal

scenes.narration: First, six borders around the world that really do make no sense. Each one is stranger than the last.
scenes.headline: Six Borders, Counting Down

scenes.narration: By the end, you'll see why India's wide open gate may be the strangest of them all.
scenes.headline: India's Is Last

scenes.narration: Every one of these is real, and you can find each of them on your phone map right now.
scenes.headline: All Real, All On Maps

scenes.narration: We start with an American place that you can only reach by road if you leave America.
scenes.headline: Leave America To Arrive

scenes.narration: Number six: Point Roberts, in Washington state. Your drive to the rest of America goes through Canada.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts, USA

scenes.narration: Point Roberts sits on the tip of a small peninsula. The land is American, but it hangs off Canada.
scenes.headline: American Land On Canada

scenes.narration: The reason is one straight line. America and Britain agreed to split their territory along the 49th parallel.
scenes.headline: One Straight Line

scenes.narration: Nobody stopped to check that this line would slice through the bottom of a peninsula.
scenes.headline: The Line Cuts Through

scenes.narration: So a small piece of the United States ended up cut off from the rest of the United States.
scenes.headline: A Piece Cut Off

scenes.narration: To drive to the rest of Washington, you leave America, cross Canadian roads, and then enter America again.
scenes.headline: Out Of USA And Back

scenes.narration: That means two border checks to go from one American town to another American town.
scenes.headline: Two Border Checks

scenes.narration: Locals still make that trip for everyday errands like shopping and work.
scenes.headline: Just Running Errands

scenes.narration: One old line drawn on a map still decides which road everyone there must take.
scenes.headline: A Line Picks Your Road

scenes.narration: That was a piece of America stuck on foreign land. Next, a village that did the opposite.
scenes.headline: Next: A German Village

scenes.narration: Number five: Büsingen am Hochrhein. This is a German village, but all around it is Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Büsingen, Germany

scenes.narration: Look at the map and you see a small German patch sitting inside Swiss land.
scenes.headline: Germany Inside Switzerland

scenes.narration: It ended up there through old deals between rulers, and later talks to change it never worked out.
scenes.headline: Old Deals, Stuck Forever

scenes.narration: Today the village is German on paper, but it sits inside the Swiss customs area.
scenes.headline: German, But Swiss Customs

scenes.narration: That means Swiss francs are part of daily life there, alongside the euro.
scenes.headline: Francs And Euros

scenes.narration: Its people follow German law, yet live inside Swiss customs rules, so every day mixes two systems.
scenes.headline: Two Systems, One Village

scenes.narration: A walk down a road can take you from Germany into Switzerland with no border check at all.
scenes.headline: No Check On The Road

scenes.narration: It is a whole German village, with homes and shops, living inside another country.
scenes.headline: A Village Inside A Country

scenes.narration: No guards, no fence, just a village that belongs to one country and sits inside another.
scenes.headline: No Fence, Still Foreign

scenes.narration: Next, a Spanish town inside France, and it exists because of one word in a treaty.
scenes.headline: One Word Changed It

scenes.narration: Number four: Llívia. This Spanish town sits inside France, with French land on every side.
scenes.headline: Llívia, Spain

scenes.narration: In 1659, Spain and France signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees to end a long war.
scenes.headline: Treaty Of The Pyrenees

scenes.narration: Spain handed over a list of villages to France as part of the deal.
scenes.headline: A List Of Villages

scenes.narration: But Llívia was a town, not a village. So by the wording of the treaty, it stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: Think about that. A single word kept a whole town on the other side of a border.
scenes.headline: A Single Word

scenes.narration: Today you can still drive there. A short road links Llívia back to Spain. It runs through France, but cars can pass freely.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: So you can drive from Spain to a Spanish town while passing over French ground.
scenes.headline: Spain To Spain Via France

scenes.narration: On the map, it looks like a drop of Spain spilled onto the French side of the mountains.
scenes.headline: A Drop Of Spain

scenes.narration: The lesson of number four: a border is sometimes just a word that nobody ever changed.
scenes.headline: A Word Nobody Changed

scenes.narration: If you enjoy facts that sound fake but are true, subscribe, because there are more of these coming.
scenes.headline: More Strange Places Coming

scenes.narration: The next one is not a village or a town. It is a whole region cut off from its own country.
scenes.headline: A Whole Region Cut Off

scenes.narration: Number three: Kaliningrad. A piece of Russia that has no land connection to the rest of Russia.
scenes.headline: Kaliningrad, Russia

scenes.narration: Look at the map and you will find it squeezed between Poland and Lithuania, with the Baltic Sea to the north.
scenes.headline: Between Poland And Lithuania

scenes.narration: Before 1945 this was the German city of Königsberg, and the famous thinker Immanuel Kant lived his whole life here.
scenes.headline: Once Königsberg

scenes.narration: After the Second World War it became part of the Soviet Union.
scenes.headline: Soviet After 1945

scenes.narration: When the Soviet Union broke up in 1991, Lithuania, Latvia and Belarus became separate countries between Kaliningrad and the rest of Russia.
scenes.headline: 1991: Everything Changed

scenes.narration: Overnight, a Russian region was sitting alone, surrounded by other countries and the sea.
scenes.headline: Alone Overnight

scenes.narration: Going by land from the rest of Russia means passing through other countries, with rules for every crossing.
scenes.headline: Rules At Every Crossing

scenes.narration: A trip inside one country can become an international trip, just because of where the lines fell.
scenes.headline: Home Trip, Foreign Land

scenes.narration: Same country, but a German past and no road home on Russian soil.
scenes.headline: No Road On Home Soil

scenes.narration: Kaliningrad is only a region, though. The next border is an entire country trapped inside another.
scenes.headline: Next: A Whole Country

scenes.narration: Number two: Lesotho. This is not a village or a region. It is an entire country, surrounded by one other.
scenes.headline: Lesotho

scenes.narration: South Africa wraps around Lesotho on every side. No sea, no third neighbour, just one country around another.
scenes.headline: One Country Around Another

scenes.narration: Lesotho has its own king, its own flag, its own money and its own seat at the United Nations.
scenes.headline: A Full Country

scenes.narration: Yet every road out of it leads into South Africa.
scenes.headline: Every Road Leads Out To SA

scenes.narration: It is called the Kingdom in the Sky, because the whole country sits high in the mountains.
scenes.headline: Kingdom In The Sky

scenes.narration: Even its lowest point is more than one thousand metres above sea level.
scenes.headline: Lowest Point: 1,000 m+

scenes.narration: Winters there bring real snow, and people even ski in a country with South Africa all around it.
scenes.headline: Snow In Africa

scenes.narration: Lesotho has just one neighbour, and that neighbour is on all sides.
scenes.headline: One Neighbour, All Sides

scenes.narration: Imagine a free country sitting inside the map of another, like a coin in a ring.
scenes.headline: A Coin In A Ring

scenes.narration: Now for number one, and it comes with a map mistake and a very big lake.
scenes.headline: A Map Mistake

scenes.narration: Number one: the Northwest Angle in Minnesota. It is American land that you can reach by road only through Canada.
scenes.headline: The Northwest Angle

scenes.narration: On a map of the United States, there is a small square sticking up from the top of Minnesota.
scenes.headline: A Square On Top

scenes.narration: It sits north of the 49th parallel, which is the line that marks much of the US-Canada border.
scenes.headline: North Of The Line

scenes.narration: It is the only part of the lower 48 states that lies north of that line.
scenes.headline: The Only One

scenes.narration: The reason goes back to 1783, when negotiators used a map that had mistakes about the rivers and lakes.
scenes.headline: A Flawed 1783 Map

scenes.narration: The treaty line was drawn using that map, and later surveys found it did not match the real land.
scenes.headline: Map Did Not Match

scenes.narration: That left a piece of Minnesota stuck on the wrong side, across a big lake.
scenes.headline: Stuck Across The Lake

scenes.narration: To reach it by road, you drive through Manitoba in Canada, then arrive back in the United States.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Manitoba

scenes.narration: Or you take a boat across the Lake of the Woods and stay on the water.
scenes.headline: Or Take A Boat

scenes.narration: A mapping mistake from 1783 is still making people use another country's roads today.
scenes.headline: A 1783 Mistake, Still Here

scenes.narration: That was number one on the list. But India has a border that is stranger in the opposite way.
scenes.headline: India's Is Different

scenes.narration: It is the India-Nepal border at Sunauli, in Uttar Pradesh. Cross it, and you arrive in Bhairahawa, Nepal.
scenes.headline: Sunauli To Bhairahawa

scenes.narration: Here the strange part is not a cut-off island. It is that you can walk across without a visa.
scenes.headline: No Visa Needed

scenes.narration: Indians and Nepalis cross on foot, by bicycle, by rickshaw, or on a bus, in front of a simple gate.
scenes.headline: Walk, Cycle, Rickshaw

scenes.narration: Shops, hotels and traffic run on both sides, with one quiet gate between two countries.
scenes.headline: One Gate, Two Countries

scenes.narration: The reason is a treaty signed in 1950, called the Treaty of Peace and Friendship.
scenes.headline: The 1950 Treaty

scenes.narration: Under it, Indians and Nepalis can travel, live and work in each other's country without a visa or work permit.
scenes.headline: Live And Work Freely

scenes.narration: Many Nepalis work in India, and many Indians have family, business and pilgrimage ties in Nepal.
scenes.headline: Families On Both Sides

scenes.narration: You should still carry a valid ID, and foreign travellers must use official crossing points with their documents.
scenes.headline: Carry Your ID

scenes.narration: A short drive from the Nepal side is Lumbini, where the Buddha was born.
scenes.headline: Lumbini Is Close

scenes.narration: Step across, and even the clock changes: Nepal is fifteen minutes ahead of Indian time.
scenes.headline: Clock Jumps 15 Minutes

scenes.narration: Most borders are made to stop you. This one is made to let you through.
scenes.headline: Made To Let You Through

scenes.narration: So the strangest border on this list is not cut off, split or lost. It is open.
scenes.headline: The Strangest Is Open

scenes.narration: From a town in Washington to a gate in Uttar Pradesh, one line on a map can change everything.
scenes.headline: One Line Changes Everything

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: a real city that sits on two continents at once.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow: Two Continents
